preconditions.description: The number of computers n is between 1 and 1500.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= a[i][j] <= (n * (n - 1)) // 2 for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
preconditions.description: Each difficulty value a[i][j] is between 0 and (n * (n - 1)) // 2.
The difficulty of sending data between a computer and itself is 0.

preconditions.expression: all(a[i][j] > 0 for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n))
preconditions.description: The difficulty of sending data between different computers is greater than 0.

preconditions.expression: all(a[i][j] == a[j][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n))
preconditions.description: The difficulty of sending data between computers i and j is the same as between j and i.

preconditions.expression: len(set(a[i][j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n))) == (n * (n - 1)) // 2
preconditions.description: All difficulty values a[i][j] for i < j are different.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= output[k] <= 998244353 for k in range(n))
postconditions.description: Each integer in the output is between 0 and 998244353.

postconditions.expression: output[k] == count_ways_to_divide_computers_into_k_groups(n, a, k) % 998244353 for k in range(n)
postconditions.description: The k-th integer in the output is the number of ways to divide computers into k groups, modulo 998244353.
